summary.text: Ayanna Pressley is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for Massachusetts's 7th District. A former congressional and Senate aide, she served on the Boston City Council from 2010 to 2019 and was elected to Congress in 2018 after defeating incumbent Michael Capuano in the Democratic primary. She is the first Black woman elected to the U.S. House from Massachusetts and is unopposed in the November 3 general election.

paragraphs.text: Born in Cincinnati, Ohio, in 1974 (February 3, according to Wikipedia), and grew up in Chicago, Illinois.

Worked as a senior aide to Congressman Joseph P. Kennedy II and Senator John Kerry before entering elected office; according to Wikipedia, she was Kennedy's scheduler and constituency director and Kerry's political director.

Served on the Boston City Council from 2010 to 2019 as an at-large member, the first Black woman elected to that body (her congressional office describes her as the first woman of color elected to the council in its 100-year history).

Elected to the U.S. House in 2018 after defeating ten-term incumbent Michael Capuano in the Democratic primary; took office January 3, 2019, as the first Black woman elected to Congress from Massachusetts.
Serves on the House Financial Services Committee and the House Oversight Committee, according to her official biography.
In 2020 publicly disclosed that she lives with alopecia, and according to her office has since worked to raise awareness of the condition.
